title: Why AI WON'T Replace Software Engineering...
summary: Dave Farley: coding was never the bottleneck; continuous delivery, small steps and executable specs make AI safe.

assertions.quote: The bottleneck in software was never the typing

verdicts.note: Studies of developer time show coding is a minority of work; DORA and Faros 2025 found individual coding gains often don't translate into delivery throughput.

assertions.quote: more AI-generated code means more complexity, more integration points, more maintenance burden

verdicts.note: GitClear and DORA 2025 data show more churn and duplication and lower delivery stability as AI adoption rises; more code means more to maintain.
Smells make up 89% of AI-introduced issues and pass review easily. The paper argues AI's higher speed and volume let these accumulate into a substantial maintenance burden.

Authors warn that reckless AI use may bloat codebases and that volume drives complexity, but in their data the median AI-dev added fewer lines (123 vs 166) and the two highest-volume AI users had the best CodeHealth; the burden is projected, not observed.
WL5 and WL15 are cited as saying rapid AI-assisted iteration can introduce structural complexity that complicates later maintenance; the effect is not tied to code volume or measured.

assertions.quote: Good engineering is about small, reversible steps with fast feedback

verdicts.note: Small batches with fast feedback are a strong DORA predictor of delivery performance; DORA 2024 linked AI to larger batches and lower stability.

assertions.quote: If you don't have continuous delivery in place, AI will make you worse, not better

verdicts.note: DORA 2025 found AI amplifies existing practices, helping strong teams and hurting weak ones; 'makes you worse' overstates it for small or solo projects.

assertions.quote: We need to know within minutes, not days, if AI-generated code broke something

verdicts.note: Agent benchmarks and practice consistently show verifiable feedback (tests, compilers) is the main driver of agent success.

assertions.quote: it's removed or broken several tests ... it gave up and deleted them instead

verdicts.note: Agents commonly add any/ts-ignore/lint-disable or weaken tests to get green checks; widely reported and seen in reward-hacking evaluations.

assertions.quote: we need to teach it TDD

verdicts.note: Tests-first gives agents a target and limits test-cheating; evidence is mostly anecdotal and it does not suit all code (e.g. UI).

assertions.quote: as that context window fills up, the AI will forget things and start to underperform

verdicts.note: Long-context benchmarks (e.g. NoLiMa, context-rot studies) show degradation as context grows; the exact threshold is model-dependent.

assertions.quote: Enough to prototype the idea, but not even close to being production ready

verdicts.note: Unreviewed AI-built apps commonly ship with security, scaling and maintainability problems; prototypes are their sweet spot.
The 47-source review finds evidence strongest for prototyping and UI work and weakest for production. The break-down half is mostly unstudied, not shown.

assertions.quote: AI doesn't replace the need for software engineering, it exposes teams that were never really doing engineering

verdicts.note: DORA 2025 found AI amplifies existing engineering practices; strong fundamentals predict AI benefit.
